items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: In the band was Harry Edison Addison, Marty Harris playing piano, John Williams playing bass

ctx.x: Yeah, yeah. How about that. But you know, the story really didn't tell the story of her life, you know, and the director sent for Harry Edison Addison and me. He wanted to interview us and to talk about Lady before they shot the movie. So we had this interview with him and we were just telling him little incidents and things, you know, about Billie and the things that he was telling us didn't quite come out. So we told him, said, that's not really Billie's story, you know. So he said, well actually we aren't…
So why even ask you questions?

items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: this thing we did with Nat, with 'After Midnight' that featured Stuff Smith, John Tizol, Willie Smith, Harry Edison, John Collins.

ctx.x: Maybe I will. I'll go out and shoot Nat Hentoff first, then I'll shoot Leonard. This is -- as I say, this is very disturbing. I can't understand this. You know, because I made records, two solos, like with the Nat -- this thing we did with Nat, with "After Midnight" that featured Stuff Smith, John Tizol, Willie Smith, Harry Edison, John Collins. And Nat. How can I -- you know, what is this? It's just amazing, I don't understand it.

items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: I was telling you about one recording I did with Ella Fitzgerald... Benny Carter was the leader, and it was Georgie Auld, Edison Georgia All, Harry Sweets Addison, and Louie Bellson.

ctx.x: You were saying earlier that someone who you recorded with wasn't stimulating musically. Who were some that you recorded with of the most stimulating people, musically, (inaudible).

Well, I was telling you about one recording I did with Ella Fitzgerald about -- I guess about two years ago. This was a unique, unusual record in that we did 30 tunes on one side, and we segued from one tune to another, never a break, just a direct segue. And it was a beautiful album. Benny Carter was the leader, and it was Georgie Auld, Edison Georgia All, Harry Sweets Addison, and Louie Bellson. We had a bass player, Bob West. Did I say Jimmie Jones was playing piano? Yeah, Jimmie Jones was playing piano. And I…
mind me about the last names because I --
